items.originalSummary: arXiv:2508.04064v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Horizontal federated learning (HFL) backdoor audits often summarize model behavior through clean accuracy (CA), mean attack success rate (ASR), or a single known-trigger test. Such summaries can hide a different failure mode, in which one target label is activated by many trigger realizations. We study this failure mode with FLAT, a latent-conditioned reliability stress test for HFL backdoors. In FLAT, compromised clients still submit ordinary classifier updates to the server, while an attacker-side generator $G(x,t,z)$ separates target intent $t$ from trigger realization $z$. This separation shifts the audit question from whether one known trigger succeeds to how the hidden behavior varies across targets, latent samples, defenses, and post-stop rounds. On CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, FLAT preserves clean utility while reaching 99.49%, 99.66%, and 94.10% single-target FedAvg ASR. The evaluation also reveals non-uniform defense responses, where a server rule can suppress one target mode while leaving another active. These observations motivate HFL backdoor audits that report target-wise ASR, worst-target ASR, target coverage, latent-sampled behavior, post-stop persistence, and defense response.

items.title: Researchers propose TANDEM, a temporal attention-guided neural differential equation model for classifying time series with missing data, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on 30 benchmarks and a medical dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: TANDEM: Temporal Attention-guided Neural Differential Equations for Missingness in Time Series Classification
items.summary:
Researchers have developed TANDEM, a temporal attention-guided neural differential equation model designed to classify time series data with missing values. This approach integrates raw observations, interpolated control paths, and continuous latent dynamics through an innovative attention mechanism, enabling the model to focus on the most informative parts of the data. TANDEM was tested on 30 benchmark datasets and a real-world medical dataset, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in classification accuracy.

Traditional methods for handling missing data in time series often rely on imputation, which can introduce bias or fail to capture temporal dynamics effectively. TANDEM addresses these challenges by combining neural differential equations with attention guidance, providing a more robust framework for managing missingness in time series classification. This advancement not only enhances predictive performance but also offers practical insights into handling incomplete data in various applications.

Researchers have developed TANDEM, a temporal attention-guided neural differential equation model designed to classify time series data with missing values. This approach integrates raw observations, interpolated control paths, and continuous latent dynamics through an innovative attention mechanism, enabling the model to focus on the most informative parts of the data. TANDEM was tested on 30 benchmark datasets and a real-world medical dataset, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in classification accuracy.

Traditional methods for handling missing data in time series often rely on imputation, which can introduce bias or fail to capture temporal dynamics effectively. TANDEM addresses these challenges by combining neural differential equations with attention guidance, providing a more robust framework for managing missingness in time series classification. This advancement not only enhances predictive performance but also offers practical insights into handling incomplete data in various applications.

items.title: Researchers present CWT-enhanced vibration sensing framework using YOLOv9-11 for localized time-frequency region detection in bearing fault monitoring, achieving up to 99.5% mAP on multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: CWT-Enhanced Vibration Sensing With Time-Frequency Region Localization Using YOLO
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a vibration sensing framework that enhances bearing fault monitoring by using continuous wavelet transform (CWT) spectrograms combined with YOLOv9, YOLOv10, and YOLOv11 models to detect localized fault-related energy regions in the time-frequency domain. This approach improves the detection of weak and non-stationary fault signatures, achieving mean average precision (mAP) scores up to 99.5% across multiple datasets including CWRU, PU, and IMS.

The framework outperforms traditional time-series models, modern vision backbones, and short-time Fourier transform (STFT)-based methods in terms of detectability and robustness. Additionally, it offers a more interpretable connection between time-frequency energy distributions and characteristic bearing fault frequencies, making it a promising tool for reliable and interpretable vibration sensing in noisy industrial environments.

items.title: Researchers introduce rBridge, a small proxy model under 1B parameters that predicts large language model reasoning performance with over 100x cost reduction and strong correlation across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Predicting LLM Reasoning Performance with Small Proxy Model
items.summary:
Researchers have developed rBridge, a small proxy model with fewer than 1 billion parameters, that can predict the reasoning performance of much larger language models with over 100 times cost reduction. rBridge aligns closely with both the pre-training objective and the target reasoning tasks by weighting negative log-likelihood with task alignment and using reasoning traces from advanced models as reference. This approach enables effective dataset optimization before scaling up to large models, which typically require over 7 billion parameters to exhibit reliable reasoning capabilities.

In experiments, rBridge demonstrated the strongest correlation with reasoning performance across six benchmarks for models ranging from 1 billion to 32 billion parameters. It also successfully transferred predictive relationships across different pre-training datasets in a zero-shot manner for models between 1 billion and 7 billion parameters. These results suggest that rBridge offers a practical and cost-efficient method for exploring reasoning-oriented pre-training in large language models.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2509.21013v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given the prohibitive cost of pre-training large language models, it is essential to leverage smaller proxy models to optimize datasets before scaling up. However, this approach becomes challenging for reasoning capabilities, which exhibit emergent behavior that only appear reliably at larger model sizes, often exceeding 7B parameters. To address this, we introduce rBridge, showing that small proxies ($\leq$1B) can effectively predict large-model reasoning by aligning more closely with (1) the pre-training objective and (2) the target task. rBridge achieves this by weighting negative log-likelihood with task alignment, using reasoning traces from frontier models as gold labels. In our experiments, rBridge (i) reduces dataset ranking costs by over 100x relative to the best baseline, (ii) achieves the strongest correlation across six reasoning benchmarks at 1B to 32B scale, and (iii) zero-shot transfers predictive relationships across pre-training datasets at 1B to 7B scale. These findings indicate that rBridge offers a practical path for exploring reasoning-oriented pre-training at lower cost.

items.title: Researchers propose K-Merge, a data-free, efficient method for online continual merging of Low-Rank Adapters on-device to support multiple tasks under storage constraints [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: K-Merge: Online Continual Merging of Adapters for On-device Large Language Models
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced K-Merge, a novel method designed for on-device deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) that efficiently merges Low-Rank Adapters (LoRAs) to support multiple tasks within limited storage constraints. This approach addresses the challenge of incrementally incorporating new LoRAs as users request support for additional tasks, ensuring that performance on previously supported tasks is maintained without requiring access to original training data.

K-Merge operates in a data-free and computationally efficient manner, selecting and merging adapters when new ones become available, while respecting the storage and computational limits typical of mobile devices. Extensive experiments on real-world tasks demonstrate that K-Merge outperforms existing strategies, making it a promising solution for continual learning and adaptation of LLMs on resource-constrained devices.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2510.13537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On-device deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently leverages Low-Rank Adapters (LoRAs) to support diverse downstream tasks under tight resource constraints. To address the limited storage capacity of mobile devices, recent works have explored model merging techniques to fuse multiple LoRAs into a single one. In practice, however, LoRAs are often delivered incrementally, as users request support for new tasks (e.g., novel problem types or languages). This scenario introduces a new challenge: on-device online continual merging, where the objective is to incorporate new LoRAs while preserving the performance on previously supported tasks. In this paper, we propose a data-free and computationally efficient strategy for selecting and merging LoRAs when a new one becomes available, assuming the device can store only a limited number of adapters. Extensive experiments across real-world tasks demonstrate the superiority of our approach compared to alternative strategies while adhering to the storage budget and compute limitations of on-device settings. The project page is available at: https://donaldssh.github.io/K-Merge.

items.title: Researchers propose FlowPath, an invertible neural flow method that learns data-driven manifolds for improved classification of irregularly-sampled time series, showing significant accuracy gains on 18 benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: FlowPath: Learning Data-Driven Manifolds with Invertible Flows for Robust Irregularly-sampled Time Series Classification
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced FlowPath, a novel method that uses invertible neural flows to learn data-driven manifolds for classifying irregularly-sampled time series. This approach improves upon traditional fixed interpolation methods by constructing continuous, data-adaptive control paths that better represent the underlying data geometry, leading to enhanced classification accuracy.

FlowPath enforces invertibility constraints to ensure information preservation and well-behaved transformations, distinguishing it from previous models that lacked such constraints. Evaluations on 18 benchmark datasets and a real-world case study demonstrate that FlowPath consistently outperforms baseline methods, highlighting the importance of modeling both the dynamics and geometry of control paths in irregular time series analysis.

These findings suggest that incorporating learned geometric structures into time series models can provide more robust and generalizable solutions, especially in scenarios with sparse or irregular data sampling. FlowPath offers a promising direction for advancing continuous-time dynamics modeling in machine learning.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2511.10841v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modeling continuous-time dynamics from sparse and irregularly-sampled time series remains a fundamental challenge. Neural controlled differential equations provide a principled framework for such tasks, yet their performance is highly sensitive to the choice of control path constructed from discrete observations. Existing methods commonly employ fixed interpolation schemes, which impose simplistic geometric assumptions that often misrepresent the underlying data manifold, particularly under high missingness. We propose FlowPath, a novel approach that learns the geometry of the control path via an invertible neural flow. Rather than merely connecting observations, FlowPath constructs a continuous and data-adaptive manifold, guided by invertibility constraints that enforce information-preserving and well-behaved transformations. This inductive bias distinguishes FlowPath from prior unconstrained learnable path models. Empirical evaluations on 18 benchmark datasets and a real-world case study demonstrate that FlowPath consistently achieves statistically significant improvements in classification accuracy over baselines using fixed interpolants or non-invertible architectures. These results highlight the importance of modeling not only the dynamics along the path but also the geometry of the path itself, offering a robust and generalizable solution for learning from irregular time series.

items.title: Researchers find 8-bit quantization improves continual learning retention and efficiency in large language models compared to FP16, with INT8 balancing plasticity and knowledge retention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: When Less is More: 8-bit Quantization Improves Continual Learning in Large Language Models
items.summary:
Researchers have found that 8-bit quantization improves continual learning retention and efficiency in large language models compared to the commonly used FP16 precision. Their study reveals that while FP16 models perform better initially, quantized models, especially those using INT8 and INT4 precision, outperform FP16 on subsequent tasks by 8-15%, with INT4 nearly doubling FP16's performance in code generation. The research highlights that even minimal replay buffers significantly enhance knowledge retention, with INT8 striking the best balance between learning adaptability and memory retention.

The team suggests that the noise introduced by quantization acts as a form of implicit regularization, reducing overfitting to new tasks that often affects higher-precision models. Their findings challenge the assumption that higher precision always yields better results, proposing that INT8 quantization offers both computational efficiency and improved continual learning dynamics. Practical guidelines from the study recommend small replay buffers for natural language understanding tasks and moderate buffers for math and code tasks, with quantized models requiring less replay to maintain performance comparable to FP16.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2512.18934v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting poses a fundamental challenge in continual learning, particularly when models are quantized for deployment efficiency. We systematically investigate the interplay between quantization precision (FP16, INT8, INT4) and replay buffer strategies in large language models, revealing unexpected dynamics. While FP16 achieves superior initial task performance (74.44% on NLU), we observe a striking inversion on subsequent tasks: quantized models outperform FP16 by 8-15% on final task forward accuracy, with INT4 achieving nearly double FP16's performance on Code generation (40% vs 20%). Critically, even minimal replay buffers (0.1%) dramatically improve retention - increasing NLU retention after Math training from 45% to 65% across all precision levels - with INT8 consistently achieving the optimal balance between learning plasticity and knowledge retention. We hypothesize that quantization-induced noise acts as implicit regularization, preventing the overfitting to new task gradients that plagues high-precision models. These findings challenge the conventional wisdom that higher precision is always preferable, suggesting instead that INT8 quantization offers both computational efficiency and superior continual learning dynamics. Our results provide practical guidelines for deploying compressed models in continual learning scenarios: small replay buffers (1-2%) suffice for NLU tasks, while Math and Code benefit from moderate buffers (5-10%), with quantized models requiring less replay than FP16 to achieve comparable retention. Code is available at https://github.com/Festyve/LessIsMore.

items.title: Researchers use AlphaEarth satellite-derived embeddings to improve hydrological model accuracy in predicting river flow in ungauged basins by capturing complex environmental patterns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Utilizing Earth Foundation Models to Enhance the Simulation Performance of Hydrological Models with AlphaEarth Embeddings
items.summary:
Researchers have demonstrated that AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings, derived from extensive satellite imagery, can improve the accuracy of hydrological models in predicting river flow in ungauged basins. These embeddings capture complex environmental patterns such as vegetation, land surface properties, and long-term dynamics more effectively than traditional basin attributes, leading to better performance in flow predictions for basins not included in training data.

The study also highlights the importance of selecting donor basins with similar environmental and hydrological characteristics based on these embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy. Incorporating many dissimilar basins was found to reduce model performance. These findings suggest that satellite-informed environmental representations can strengthen hydrological forecasting and facilitate the development of adaptable models for diverse landscapes.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2601.01558v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Predicting river flow in places without streamflow records is challenging because basins respond differently to climate, terrain, vegetation, and soils. Traditional basin attributes describe some of these differences, but they cannot fully represent the complexity of natural environments. This study examines whether AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings, which are learned from large collections of satellite images rather than designed by experts, offer a more informative way to describe basin characteristics. These embeddings summarize patterns in vegetation, land surface properties, and long-term environmental dynamics. We find that models using them achieve higher accuracy when predicting flows in basins not used for training, suggesting that they capture key physical differences more effectively than traditional attributes. We further investigate how selecting appropriate donor basins influences prediction in ungauged regions. Similarity based on the embeddings helps identify basins with comparable environmental and hydrological behavior, improving performance, whereas adding many dissimilar basins can reduce accuracy. The results show that satellite-informed environmental representations can strengthen hydrological forecasting and support the development of models that adapt more easily to different landscapes.

items.title: Researchers introduce KAGE-Bench, a fast JAX-native benchmark isolating visual generalization failures in pixel-based reinforcement learning with 34 train-evaluation pairs and up to 33M steps per second [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: KAGE-Bench: Fast Known-Axis Visual Generalization Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning
items.summary:
Researchers have developed KAGE-Bench, a JAX-native benchmark designed to isolate and evaluate visual generalization failures in pixel-based reinforcement learning agents. The benchmark is built on KAGE-Env, a 2D platformer environment that separates visual factors into independently controllable axes while maintaining consistent underlying control tasks. KAGE-Bench includes 34 train-evaluation pairs across six visual shift categories, enabling precise analysis of how different visual changes impact agent performance.

Using a standard PPO-CNN baseline, the study found that certain visual shifts, such as changes in background and lighting, significantly impair agent success, whereas alterations in agent appearance have less effect. Some visual changes allowed agents to maintain forward movement but prevented task completion, indicating that reward metrics alone may not fully capture generalization issues. The fully vectorized JAX implementation supports up to 33 million environment steps per second on a single GPU, facilitating rapid and reproducible testing across visual variations.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2601.14232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pixel-based reinforcement learning agents often fail under purely visual distribution shift even when latent dynamics and rewards are unchanged, but existing benchmarks entangle multiple sources of shift and hinder systematic analysis. We introduce KAGE-Env, a JAX-native 2D platformer that factorizes the observation process into independently controllable visual axes while keeping the underlying control problem fixed. By construction, varying a visual axis affects performance only through the induced state-conditional action distribution of a pixel policy, providing a clean abstraction for visual generalization. Building on this environment, we define KAGE-Bench, a benchmark of six known-axis suites comprising 34 train-evaluation configuration pairs that isolate individual visual shifts. Using a standard PPO-CNN baseline, we observe strong axis-dependent failures, with background and photometric shifts often collapsing success, while agent-appearance shifts are comparatively benign. Several shifts preserve forward motion while breaking task completion, showing that return alone can obscure generalization failures. Finally, the fully vectorized JAX implementation enables up to 33M environment steps per second on a single GPU, enabling fast and reproducible sweeps over visual factors. Code: https://avanturist322.github.io/KAGEBench/.

items.title: PaAno proposes lightweight patch-based representation learning for time-series anomaly detection, achieving state-of-the-art results on TSB-AD benchmark with faster, more efficient inference than transformer-based models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: PaAno: Patch-Based Representation Learning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced PaAno, a lightweight patch-based representation learning method for time-series anomaly detection that achieves state-of-the-art results on the TSB-AD benchmark. Unlike recent approaches relying on large neural networks such as transformers, PaAno uses a 1D convolutional neural network to embed short temporal patches from training data, enabling faster and more efficient inference suitable for real-time and resource-constrained environments.

PaAno is trained with a combination of triplet loss and pretext loss to capture meaningful temporal patterns in the data. During inference, it computes anomaly scores by comparing embeddings of patches around each time step to those of normal patches from training data. Evaluations show that PaAno significantly outperforms existing methods, including heavy architectures, on both univariate and multivariate time-series anomaly detection across various performance metrics.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2602.01359v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although recent studies on time-series anomaly detection have increasingly adopted ever-larger neural network architectures such as transformers and foundation models, they incur high computational costs and memory usage, making them impractical for real-time and resource-constrained scenarios. Moreover, they often fail to demonstrate significant performance gains over simpler methods under rigorous evaluation protocols. In this study, we propose Patch-based representation learning for time-series Anomaly detection (PaAno), a lightweight yet effective method for fast and efficient time-series anomaly detection. PaAno extracts short temporal patches from time-series training data and uses a 1D convolutional neural network to embed each patch into a vector representation. The model is trained using a combination of triplet loss and pretext loss to ensure the embeddings capture informative temporal patterns from input patches. During inference, the anomaly score at each time step is computed by comparing the embeddings of its surrounding patches to those of normal patches extracted from the training time-series. Evaluated on the TSB-AD benchmark, PaAno achieved state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing methods, including those based on heavy architectures, on both univariate and multivariate time-series anomaly detection across various range-wise and point-wise performance measures.

items.title: Researchers propose calibrated test-time guidance methods for Bayesian inference, correcting posterior sampling errors and improving black hole image reconstruction PSNR [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Calibrated Test-Time Guidance for Bayesian Inference
items.summary:
Researchers have identified that common test-time guidance methods used in pretrained diffusion models do not accurately sample from the true Bayesian posterior, resulting in miscalibrated inference. They analyzed the structural approximations causing this issue and proposed new estimators that enable calibrated sampling from the Bayesian posterior, improving the accuracy of Bayesian inference.

Their approach significantly outperforms existing methods across various Bayesian inference tasks and achieves a new state-of-the-art peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) in black hole image reconstruction, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing image quality in this complex application.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2602.22428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Test-time guidance is a widely used mechanism for steering pretrained diffusion models toward outcomes specified by a reward function. Existing approaches, however, focus on maximizing reward rather than sampling from the true Bayesian posterior, leading to miscalibrated inference. In this work, we show that common test-time guidance methods do not recover the correct posterior distribution and identify the structural approximations responsible for this failure. We then propose consistent alternative estimators that enable calibrated sampling from the Bayesian posterior. We significantly outperform previous methods on a set of Bayesian inference tasks, and set a new state-of-the-art PSNR in black hole image reconstruction.

items.title: Researchers develop competition-aware CPC forecasting model using 1.66 billion Google Ads records for car rental market, improving accuracy up to 27.6% over 12 weeks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Competition-Aware CPC Forecasting with Near-Market Coverage
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a competition-aware forecasting model for cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search advertising, using 1.66 billion Google Ads records from the car rental market between 2021 and 2023. The model integrates semantic keyword relationships, behavioral patterns from CPC trajectories, and geographic market data to improve prediction accuracy. It outperforms traditional statistical and machine learning baselines, achieving up to a 27.6% reduction in forecasting error over a 12-week horizon, particularly for high-CPC, high-volatility keywords where accurate predictions are most critical.

The study constructs a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks and employs spatiotemporal graph forecasting techniques that incorporate competition-aware proxies derived from keyword text, CPC trends, and localized demand. The model's effectiveness is supported by tests showing that its gains are specific to competitive dynamics rather than generic smoothing effects. These findings highlight the importance of considering competitive interactions in auction-driven advertising markets under partial observability and suggest a horizon-dependent approach to CPC forecasting.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2603.13059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search is an auction-generated outcome shaped by a competitive landscape that is only partially observable from any single advertiser's history. From 1.66 billion Google Ads log records for a concentrated car-rental market (2021-2023), we construct a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks (218,924 keyword-week observations) and build competition-aware proxies from keyword text, CPC trajectories, and geographic market structure. The design combines (i) semantic neighborhoods and a semantic keyword graph from pretrained transformer-based keyword representations, (ii) behavioral neighborhoods from Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) alignment of CPC trajectories, and (iii) geographic-intent covariates capturing localized demand and marketplace heterogeneity. We evaluate these signals both as exogenous covariates and as relational priors in spatiotemporal graph forecasters, benchmarking them against statistical, neural, and time-series foundation-model baselines. The results reveal a clear horizon crossover. At one week, graph-based models achieve the lowest error, reducing sMAPE by 15.1% relative to the strongest classical/ML baseline; at the six- and twelve-week horizons, covariate-augmented foundation models dominate, reducing sMAPE by 22.5% and 27.6%, respectively. The gains concentrate in the high-CPC, high-volatility keywords where forecasting errors are most costly. A falsification battery supports the competition interpretation at the planning horizon: the semantic competition graph outperforms a confounder-matched non-competitive graph by 4.05 sMAPE points, and matched-neighbour and time-shuffled controls show the six-week gains are competition-specific rather than generic smoothing. Together, the findings establish a horizon-dependent competition-aware forecasting design for auction-driven advertising markets under partial observability.

items.title: Researchers propose DeLL framework using dynamic knowledge spaces and causal inference to improve lifelong learning and adaptability in end-to-end autonomous driving systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Deconfounded Lifelong Learning for Autonomous Driving via Dynamic Knowledge Spaces
items.summary:
Researchers have developed DeLL, a Deconfounded Lifelong Learning framework designed to enhance end-to-end autonomous driving systems by addressing challenges such as catastrophic forgetting, knowledge transfer difficulties, and spurious correlations caused by unobservable confounders. DeLL integrates a Dirichlet process mixture model to create dynamic knowledge spaces for clustering driving behaviors and discovering latent abilities, combined with a causal inference technique called front-door adjustment to mitigate misleading correlations and improve learned representations.

The framework allows adaptive knowledge expansion without predefined cluster numbers, reducing forgetting and improving adaptability to new driving scenarios. An evolutionary trajectory decoder supports non-autoregressive planning, and new evaluation protocols based on Bench2Drive assess lifelong learning performance. Tests in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that DeLL significantly boosts driving performance and knowledge retention in autonomous driving systems.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2603.14354v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: End-to-End autonomous driving (E2E-AD) systems face challenges in lifelong learning, including catastrophic forgetting, difficulty in knowledge transfer across diverse scenarios, and spurious correlations between unobservable confounders and true driving intents. To address these issues, we propose DeLL, a Deconfounded Lifelong Learning framework that integrates a Dirichlet process mixture model (DPMM) with the front-door adjustment mechanism from causal inference. The DPMM is employed to construct two dynamic knowledge spaces: a trajectory knowledge space for clustering explicit driving behaviors and an implicit feature knowledge space for discovering latent driving abilities. Leveraging the non-parametric Bayesian nature of DPMM, our framework enables adaptive expansion and incremental updating of knowledge without predefining the number of clusters, thereby mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Meanwhile, the front-door adjustment mechanism utilizes the DPMM-derived knowledge as mediators to deconfound spurious correlations, such as those induced by sensor noise or environmental changes, and enhances the causal expressiveness of the learned representations. Additionally, we introduce an evolutionary trajectory decoder that enables non-autoregressive planning. To evaluate the lifelong learning performance of E2E-AD, we propose new evaluation protocols and metrics based on Bench2Drive. Extensive evaluations in the closed-loop CARLA simulator demonstrate that our framework significantly improves adaptability to new driving scenarios and overall driving performance, while effectively retaining previously acquired knowledge. Code: https://github.com/Mooncakebro/DeLL

items.title: Researchers propose Mutual Information Preference Optimization to improve LLM performance by 3-51% without additional data using contrastive data augmentation and direct preference optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Maximizing Mutual Information Between Prompt and Response Improves LLM Performance With No Additional Data
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced Mutual Information Preference Optimization (MIPO), a novel method to enhance large language model (LLM) performance by maximizing mutual information between prompts and responses without requiring additional data. MIPO uses contrastive data augmentation to create preference pairs, generating positive responses based on correct prompts and negative responses from unrelated prompts, and applies Direct Preference Optimization to learn from these pairs. Experiments with Llama and Qwen instruct models demonstrate performance improvements ranging from 3% to 51%, including gains in both personalized and verifiable tasks such as math and multiple-choice question answering.

This approach addresses limitations of current post-training methods that depend heavily on costly human-labeled data or external verification, offering a self-improvement framework that leverages intrinsic signals within the model. The results suggest that MIPO can effectively boost LLM capabilities across diverse domains without external supervision, pointing to a promising direction for future research in model optimization and autonomous learning.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2603.19294v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While post-training has successfully improved large language models (LLMs) across a variety of domains, these gains heavily rely on human-labeled data or external verifiers. We propose **Mutual Information Preference Optimization (MIPO)**, a contrastive data augmentation method that constructs preference pairs by generating a positive response conditioning on the correct prompt, and a negative response by conditioning on a random, unrelated prompt. We show that using Direct Preference Optimization to learn from this paired data maximizes pointwise mutual information *under the base LLM* between prompts and model responses. Experiments with with 1-7B parameter Llama and Qwen instruct models show that MIPO achieves 3-16% gains (and 51% increase for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) on personalization compared to prompting baselines. Surprisingly, MIPO can also be useful in verifiable domains, such as math and multiple-choice question answering, yielding 1-20% gains *without any additional data or external supervision*. These results suggest a promising direction for self-improvement using intrinsic signals derived from contrastive data pairs.

items.title: Researchers present Crystalite, a lightweight diffusion Transformer with Subatomic Tokenization and Geometry Enhancement Module for efficient crystal modeling, achieving state-of-the-art prediction and faster sampling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Crystalite: A Lightweight Transformer for Efficient Crystal Modeling
items.summary:
Researchers have developed Crystalite, a lightweight diffusion Transformer designed for efficient crystal modeling. This model introduces two key innovations: Subatomic Tokenization, which offers a compact and chemically structured atom representation, and the Geometry Enhancement Module (GEM), which incorporates periodic geometric information directly into the attention mechanism. These features enable Crystalite to maintain the simplicity and efficiency of standard Transformers while better capturing the structure of crystalline materials.

Crystalite achieves state-of-the-art performance on crystal structure prediction benchmarks and excels in de novo crystal generation, attaining the highest S.U.N. discovery score among evaluated methods. Additionally, it samples significantly faster than existing geometry-intensive models, offering a more efficient approach to generative modeling of crystalline materials.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2604.02270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generative models for crystalline materials often rely on equivariant graph neural networks, which capture geometric structure well but are costly to train and slow to sample. The first is Subatomic Tokenization, a compact chemically structured atom representation that replaces high-dimensional one-hot encodings and is better suited to continuous diffusion. The second is the Geometry Enhancement Module (GEM), which injects periodic minimum-image pair geometry directly into attention through additive geometric biases. Together, these components preserve the simplicity and efficiency of a standard Transformer while making it better matched to the structure of crystalline materials. Crystalite achieves state-of-the-art results on crystal structure prediction benchmarks, and de novo generation performance, attaining the best S.U.N. discovery score among the evaluated baselines while sampling substantially faster than geometry-heavy alternatives.

items.title: Researchers introduce GUI-Perturbed framework revealing systematic accuracy drops in GUI grounding models on spatial reasoning tasks and visual perturbations, releasing dataset and fine-tuned model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
items.summary:
Researchers have developed GUI-Perturbed, a framework that reveals significant accuracy declines in GUI grounding models when handling spatial reasoning tasks and visual perturbations. While these models typically achieve over 85% accuracy on standard benchmarks, their performance drops by 27 to 56 percentage points with relational instructions requiring spatial understanding. The framework independently varies visual scenes and instructions to assess robustness, uncovering systematic accuracy collapses across three evaluated 7B models and notable degradation under visual changes like browser zoom.

The study highlights that current benchmarks, which test each screenshot with a single fixed instruction, fail to detect these weaknesses. Additionally, attempts to improve performance through rank-8 LoRA fine-tuning with augmented data unexpectedly reduced accuracy. By isolating specific capability axes such as spatial reasoning and visual robustness, GUI-Perturbed provides diagnostic insights beyond aggregate benchmarks. The researchers have released the dataset, augmentation pipeline, and a fine-tuned model to support further investigation and development in this area.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2604.14262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: GUI grounding models report over 85% accuracy on standard benchmarks, yet drop 27-56 percentage points when instructions require spatial reasoning rather than direct element naming. Current benchmarks miss this because they evaluate each screenshot once with a single fixed instruction. We introduce GUI-Perturbed, a controlled perturbation framework that independently varies visual scenes and instructions to measure grounding robustness. Evaluating three 7B models from the same architecture lineage, we find that relational instructions cause systematic accuracy collapse across all models, a 70% browser zoom produces statistically significant degradation, and rank-8 LoRA fine-tuning with augmented data degrades performance rather than improving it. By perturbing along independent axes, GUI-Perturbed isolates which specific capability axes are affected-spatial reasoning, visual robustness, reasoning calibration-providing diagnostic signal that aggregate benchmarks cannot. We release the dataset, augmentation pipeline, and a fine-tuned model.

items.title: Researchers propose Fed-FSTQ, a Fisher-guided token quantization method that reduces uplink traffic by 46x and speeds federated fine-tuning of large language models on edge devices by 52% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: FED-FSTQ: Fisher-Guided Token Quantization for Communication-Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs on Edge Devices
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced Fed-FSTQ, a Fisher-guided token quantization method designed to enhance communication efficiency in federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices. This approach significantly reduces uplink traffic by 46 times and accelerates training speed by 52%, addressing challenges posed by heterogeneous bandwidth and intermittent device participation in mobile environments.

Fed-FSTQ uses a lightweight Fisher information proxy to assess token importance, enabling selective token transmission with mixed-precision quantization that prioritizes critical information while minimizing redundant data. The method integrates seamlessly with existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning frameworks like LoRA without altering server aggregation and supports clients with varying bandwidth through compact sparse message packing. Experiments on multilingual and medical question-answering tasks under non-independent and identically distributed data conditions demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing communication overhead and improving training efficiency.

Additionally, applying Fisher-guided token reduction during inference yields up to a 1.55-fold speedup on resource-constrained edge devices such as NVIDIA Jetson, highlighting Fed-FSTQ's practical deployability in real-world scenarios with limited computational resources.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2604.25421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated fine-tuning provides a practical route to adapt large language models (LLMs) on edge devices without centralizing private data, yet in mobile deployments the training wall-clock is often bottlenecked by straggler-limited uplink communication under heterogeneous bandwidth and intermittent participation. Although parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) reduces trainable parameters, per-round payloads remain prohibitive in non-IID regimes, where uniform compression can discard rare but task-critical signals. We propose Fed-FSTQ, a Fisher-guided token quantization system primitive for communication-efficient federated LLM fine-tuning. Fed-FSTQ employs a lightweight Fisher proxy to estimate token sensitivity, coupling importance-aware token selection with non-uniform mixed-precision quantization to allocate higher fidelity to informative evidence while suppressing redundant transmission. The method is model-agnostic, serves as a drop-in module for standard federated PEFT pipelines, e.g., LoRA, without modifying the server aggregation rule, and supports bandwidth-heterogeneous clients via compact sparse message packing. Experiments on multilingual QA and medical QA under non-IID partitions show that Fed-FSTQ reduces cumulative uplink traffic required to reach a fixed quality threshold by 46x relative to a standard LoRA baseline, and improves end-to-end wall-clock time-to-accuracy by 52%. Furthermore, enabling Fisher-guided token reduction at inference yields up to a 1.55x end-to-end speedup on NVIDIA Jetson-class edge devices, demonstrating deployability under tight resource constraints.

items.title: Korzhinskii-Net physics-informed neural network models subsurface mineral prospectivity across six ore provinces, outperforming classical baselines with open-source pipeline [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Korzhinskii-Net: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Sub-Surface Mineral Prospectivity Modelling
items.summary:
Korzhinskii-Net is a physics-informed neural network designed to improve subsurface mineral prospectivity modeling by integrating physical processes such as Darcy flow, heat transport, and reaction rates into a differentiable forward model. Tested across six ore provinces with different commodity types, it significantly outperforms traditional data-driven classifiers, achieving a mean PR-AUC of 0.708 compared to 0.235 for the best classical baseline. This approach leverages surface and remote-sensing data while capturing subsurface physics that conventional models often overlook.

The model is named after Dmitri S. Korzhinskii, whose theory of infiltration metasomatism underpins the physical framework. Evaluations used a rigorous cross-validation protocol with controlled data leakage and disabled baseline proxy features, confirming consistent improvements across diverse geological settings. The full pipeline and evaluation tools have been released as open source, enabling further research and application in mineral exploration.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.13695v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mineral prospectivity modelling (MPM) underpins exploration economics, yet most operational pipelines reduce to data-driven classifiers trained on shallow surface proxies. Such models are blind to the subsurface physics that actually localises ore: heat advection, fluid flow, and lithology-dependent precipitation. We present Korzhinskii-Net, a 2-D radial physics-informed neural network (PINN) that couples Darcy flow, advective-diffusive heat transport, and a softplus-saturated reaction rate into a single differentiable forward model, weakly supervised by surface and remote-sensing proxies. The network is named after Dmitri S. Korzhinskii (1899-1985), whose theory of infiltration metasomatism provides the physical scaffold. We evaluate Korzhinskii-Net on six ore provinces spanning three commodity classes - Udokan (sandstone-hosted Cu), Sukhoi Log, Olimpiada, and Berezovskoye (orogenic Au), Vorontsovskoye (Carlin-type Au), and Dalnegorsk (skarn polymetallic) - under a fair, leakage-controlled 5-fold cross-validation protocol with hard ring-shaped negatives and baseline proxy features disabled. Korzhinskii-Net attains a mean PR-AUC of 0.708 versus 0.235 for the strongest classical baseline (support vector machine), and a mean fractional rank of 0.036 versus 0.475. The improvement is consistent across all six provinces and three commodity systems, suggesting that physics-informed differentiable simulators, even when constrained only by global open-data proxies, can recover localisation patterns that pure feature-based learners systematically miss. We release the full pipeline and evaluation harness as open source.

items.title: Researchers introduce Topological Neural Dynamics, a neuron-wise sequence modeling framework that outperforms RNN, LSTM, and Transformer baselines in behavior cloning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Topological Neural Dynamics: A Neuron-wise Framework for Sequence Modeling
items.summary:
Researchers have developed Topological Neural Dynamics (TND), a novel sequence modeling framework that shifts from traditional layer-wise dynamics to neuron-wise dynamics, allowing each neuron to evolve independently within a directed graph structure. This approach contrasts with existing models like RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers, which use shared operators for all neurons in a layer. items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.21295v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing sequence models, including RNNs, LSTMs, continuous-time networks, and Transformers, share a common structural principle: layer-wise dynamics, where all neurons in the same layer co-evolve through a shared parameterized operator, leaving individual neurons no freedom to evolve independently. Yet in many complex dynamical systems, rich global behavior emerges precisely from locally evolving units interacting through structured connectivity. Inspired by this principle, we introduce Topological Neural Dynamics (TND), a sequence modeling framework that shifts computation from layer-wise to neuron-wise dynamics. TND represents a neural system as a directed neuron graph, an interaction operator, and a local dynamics function, where each neuron evolves independently and collective computation emerges from interactions through the explicit graph topology. We instantiate TND as a discrete-time graph-coupled dynamical system and evaluate it as a case study on a behavior cloning task in single-player Pong. Compared with Vanilla RNN, Sparse RNN, LSTM, Closed-form continuous-time neural network (CfC), and Transformer baselines, TND achieves the best catch rate and a mean of 17.47 consecutive catches per round, more than three times that of the strongest baseline. These results suggest that shifting from layer-wise to neuron-wise dynamics provides an effective inductive bias for sequence modeling.

items.title: Study finds safety guardrails in eight large language models fail up to 100% for several mental health conditions, raising concerns over their use in public settings [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!
items.summary:
A recent study evaluated eight proprietary large language models (LLMs) for their safety in handling mental health-related conversations across 16 DSM-5 conditions. The research found that while safeguards were generally effective for suicide and self-harm, they failed completely for several other conditions, including eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder, with failure rates reaching up to 100%. This raises significant concerns about the reliability of these models in sensitive public settings such as schools, search engines, and consumer chatbots.

The study introduced a comprehensive harm taxonomy and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework to assess the models under various adversarial attacks. The findings highlight the inconsistency and inadequacy of current safety measures, emphasizing the need for clearly defined harm categories and robust safeguards tailored to different clinical conditions. Until such improvements are implemented, the use of these LLMs in public-facing applications poses considerable risks to vulnerable populations.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.23884v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health-related conversations, yet safety guardrails remain inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions. This study evaluates eight proprietary LLMs across 16 DSM-5 conditions using four adversarial attack variants, introducing an eight-dimension harm taxonomy and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Results show that safeguards hold reliably only for suicide and self-harm, while conditions such as eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder exhibit failure rates of up to 100%. We argue that ethical design and deployment of these LLMs demand clearly defined harm categories across clinical conditions and implementation of safeguards accordingly. Until such safeguards are in place, these models pose significant risks to vulnerable populations, making their growing integration into publicly available settings (e.g., schools, search engines, and consumer chatbots) are particularly concerning.

items.title: Researchers propose a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to reduce word error rate by up to 55% and enhance robustness in automatic speech recognition systems across four architectures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to improve the robustness of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, achieving up to a 55% reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) across four different architectures. This approach addresses the challenge of detecting errors in deployed ASR systems without access to true transcriptions by using a Two-Sided Atomic Audit to certify token existence and adversarial exclusion, combined with a Rank-Based Tournament to select the best transcription sequence.

The method enhances acoustic security by providing detailed word- and sentence-level certifications, increasing recall, and reducing the correlation between confidence scores and errors. This advancement offers a promising direction for making ASR systems more reliable against both adversarial and benign perturbations in real-world applications.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.27698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition systems are notoriously both sensitive to adversarial and benign perturbations. While this has been repeatedly demonstrated using reference datasets, detecting such behaviors in deployed systems is incredibly challenging, due to the absence of oracle knowledge of the true transcription. We demonstrate that employing a certification-inspired mechanism can significantly decrease WER, increase recall, and decrease the Spearman correlation between confidence and WER. We achieve this through a dual-gate diagnostic pipeline: a Two-Sided Atomic Audit that accumulates statistical wealth to certify both token existence and adversarial exclusion, and a Rank-Based Tournament that selects the winning sequence. Our evaluations across four diverse architectures demonstrate up to a 55% relative reduction in Word Error Rate, while also providing granular word- and sentence-level certifications to enhance acoustic security.

items.title: Researchers simulate over 8 million over-the-air acoustic attacks, revealing up to 94.5% word error rate increases and introducing a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio to separate source stealth from attack efficacy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Room for Error: Large-Scale Simulation of Over-the-Air Acoustic Attacks
items.summary:
Researchers have conducted over 8 million simulations of over-the-air acoustic attacks on voice-controlled AI systems, revealing that such attacks can increase word error rates by up to 94.5% in models like Whisper and wav2vec. They introduced a novel Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio metric to distinguish between the stealthiness of the attack source and the effectiveness of the attack itself, addressing a key limitation in previous studies.

The study highlights the challenges of translating digital adversarial attacks into the physical acoustic environment, which has often been oversimplified in prior research. By using a high-throughput simulation framework combined with real-world testing, the researchers provide a more accurate understanding of the risks posed by acoustic attacks and establish a foundation for reproducible and verifiable research that fully incorporates acoustic factors.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.27701v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While voice control is rapidly becoming a ubiquitous vector of human-AI communication, the risks facing these systems remain poorly understood. This is, in part, a product of the difficulties in scaling strictly digital adversarial workflows to the physical world. These scale barriers have led the community to abstract away key acoustic factors relating to detectability and the influence of geometry on acoustics. These methodological and metrological shortcomings undermine our understanding of risk. We illuminate these issues through real-world testing, conceptual discussions, and a novel, high-throughput reality simulation framework. By testing over 8 million adversarial evaluations, we demonstrate that acoustic awareness yields relative Word Error Rate increases of up to 94.5\% under Whisper and wav2vec. We employ this framework to explore a formalize and operationalize a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio to decouple source stealth from victim attack efficacy, resolving a crucial limitation in current works. This lays the groundwork for repeatable, verifiable research that embraces, rather than abstracts, the acoustic environment.

items.title: Researchers propose Training-Free Gated Reranking to reduce computational costs by up to 80% and improve few-shot learning performance by up to 2% across 8 LLMs and multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: When Reranking Hurts: Uncertainty-Based Gating for Few-Shot Reranking
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced Training-Free Gated Reranking, a method that selectively applies reranking to few-shot learning examples based on model uncertainty. This approach challenges the common assumption that reranking always enhances performance, showing that it can sometimes degrade results. Experiments involving eight large language models across multiple natural language understanding and machine translation datasets demonstrate that this method reduces computational costs by 15% to 80% while improving average performance by up to 2%.

The study highlights that higher computational expense does not necessarily lead to better outcomes and that reranking is most effective when focused on instances where the model exhibits high uncertainty. This targeted strategy offers a more efficient use of resources in few-shot learning scenarios without sacrificing, and often improving, model accuracy.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.31087v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Few-shot selection typically assumes that reranking retrieved examples always improves performance. We challenge this view by identifying that the expensive reranking step can in fact degrade performance. Instead, we propose \emph{Training-Free Gated Reranking}, which decides whether to rerank the few-shot examples based on the model's uncertainty. Extensive experiments across 8 LLMs, covering 7 NLU datasets and 9 MT domain-language combinations, demonstrate that our approach reduces computational costs by 15\%-80\% while improving average performance by up to 2\%. These findings indicate that higher computational cost does not guarantee better performance, and that reranking is most beneficial when targeted at high-uncertainty instances.

items.title: Researchers introduce FinPersona-Bench to measure mandate salience decay in autonomous financial agents using 18 LLMs with varying behavioral profiles in simulated market scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents
items.summary:
Researchers have developed FinPersona-Bench, a simulation benchmark designed to measure Mandate Salience Decay (MSD) in autonomous financial agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). MSD refers to the gradual loss of influence of explicit behavioral mandates, such as capital preservation or avoiding speculative bets, as market context accumulates over time. The benchmark evaluates 18 LLMs with varying behavioral profiles in synthetic market scenarios that separate observable prices from hidden fundamental values, testing for failures like trading without signals, panic-selling during crashes, and ignoring fundamentals during bubbles.

The study found that MSD increases over time and varies by model, with significant behavioral differences emerging between agents that receive periodic mandate re-grounding and those that do not, especially during market crashes. While re-grounding mandates benefits conservative agents in low-signal markets, it can worsen performance for aggressive agents under the same conditions. These results highlight the need for selective, mandate-aware re-grounding strategies tailored to agent profiles and market environments to ensure reliable long-term deployment of autonomous financial agents.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2606.31522v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous financial agents initialized with explicit behavioral mandates such as "preserve capital" or "avoid speculative bets" that are meant to govern every decision throughout deployment. In practice, however, as market context accumulates over long horizons, these mandates gradually lose their behavioral influence, a phenomenon we formalize as Mandate Salience Decay (MSD). To measure MSD objectively, we introduce FinPersona-Bench, a simulation benchmark in which a synthetic market decouples observable price from hidden fundamental value, enabling falsifiable evaluation across three failure modes: trading without signal in calm markets, panic-selling during crashes, and ignoring fundamental value during speculative bubbles. Evaluating 18 leading frontier and open-source LLMs, each assigned one of three behavioral profiles ranging from strict capital preservation to aggressive growth, shows that MSD compounds over time and is model-dependent. In crash scenarios, the behavioral gap between static agents and those receiving periodic mandate re-grounding grows 4.4x from the first to the final quarter of the simulation. The effects of mandate re-grounding are not uniformly positive: it consistently helps conservative agents in low-signal markets but actively worsens behavior for aggressive agents in the same setting. These findings suggest that reliable long-horizon deployment requires selective, mandate-aware re-grounding based on agent profile and market regime.

items.title: Researchers introduce Constructive Alignment paradigm to govern evolving human preference dynamics in human-AI interaction using a control-theoretic framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Constructive Alignment: Governing Preference Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction
items.summary:
Researchers propose a new paradigm called Constructive Alignment to address the dynamic nature of human preferences in human-AI interactions. Unlike traditional AI alignment approaches that treat preferences as fixed targets, this framework views preferences as evolving and shaped through ongoing interaction with adaptive AI systems. Using a control-theoretic model, the approach focuses on guiding the development of human values over time rather than merely satisfying static preferences.

The Constructive Alignment paradigm draws on insights from behavioral economics, psychology, and social theory to model preferences as layered states influenced by AI actions and interaction design. It emphasizes regulating how AI systems affect human evaluative states to ensure that evolving preferences remain coherent, reflectively endorsed, epistemically grounded, resistant to manipulation, and empowering under uncertainty. This shift reframes alignment as governing long-term value formation in human-AI relationships.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most approaches to AI alignment treat human preferences as fixed targets to be inferred and optimized. This assumption conflicts with extensive empirical evidence showing that preferences are layered, dynamic, and constructed through interaction--particularly with adaptive technologies. As AI systems become more persistent, personalized, and socially embedded, they increasingly participate in shaping what people attend to, value, and endorse over time. We introduce Constructive Alignment, a paradigm that reframes alignment as a control problem over evolving human preference trajectories rather than static preference satisfaction. Drawing on behavioral economics, psychology, and constructivist social theory, we model preferences as layered state variables that evolve under interaction with AI systems. We formalize this view using a control-theoretic framework in which system actions and interaction design jointly influence both world states and human evaluative states. We argue that alignment is not primarily about controlling AI behavior, but about regulating how AI systems influence the evolution of human preferences--ensuring that value trajectories remain coherent, reflectively endorsed, epistemically grounded, bounded against manipulation, and empowering under uncertainty. Alignment thus becomes a problem of governing long-term value formation rather than simply satisfying static preferences.

items.title: Researchers propose Bounded Morality framework to analyze computational limits of moral reasoning in finite agents, defining tradeoffs between moral breadth and depth for AI alignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Bounded Morality: Defining the Space of Moral Computation
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced the Bounded Morality framework to analyze the computational challenges of moral reasoning in finite agents. This framework extends the concept of bounded rationality by defining moral situations along two dimensions: moral breadth, which covers the range of entities considered morally relevant, and moral depth, which involves the complexity of evaluating their interactions. The study highlights an inherent tradeoff between these dimensions due to limited computational resources, framing ethical theories as strategies optimized for different conditions rather than absolute moral truths.

The framework also introduces formal concepts of moral regret and moral progress within these constraints, suggesting that effective moral alignment in artificial intelligence depends more on how moral reasoning capacity is scaled and allocated than on simply mimicking human moral judgments. This approach offers a new perspective on designing AI systems capable of nuanced ethical decision-making under resource limitations.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moral cognition has traditionally been modeled as adherence to fixed ethical theories--deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics--implemented as static rules or value functions. We propose Bounded Morality, a formal framework for analyzing the computational demands of moral problems faced by finite agents. Extending Herbert Simon's notion of bounded rationality, we formalize moral situations along two orthogonal dimensions: moral breadth, the scope of entities treated as morally relevant, and moral depth, the inferential integration required to evaluate their interactions. Limited resources impose an unavoidable tradeoff between these dimensions, defining a feasible space of moral computation. Within this space, ethical theories correspond to locally efficient strategies adapted to different demand regimes rather than competing accounts of moral truth. The framework yields a formal notion of moral regret and moral progress under constraint, and implies that moral alignment in artificial systems depends on the scaling and allocation of moral reasoning capacity rather than on direct imitation of human judgments.

items.title: Researchers present MMM data model for knowledge interoperability in decentralizable knowledge commons, combining normative constraints with free-text labels and demonstrating early usability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: The MMM Data Model -- A Normative Specification for Knowledge Interoperability in a Decentralisable Knowledge Commons
items.summary:
Researchers have introduced MMM, a new data model designed to improve knowledge interoperability within decentralizable knowledge commons. MMM addresses limitations of traditional document-centric systems by combining a small set of normative constraints with the flexibility of free-text labels, enabling interdisciplinary collaboration without requiring strict semantic alignment. The model aims to balance formal structure with human usability, supporting knowledge documentation across various disciplines and applications.

The development of MMM stems from practical needs in interdisciplinary research and is positioned within a broader analysis of information system design. A reference implementation and pilot deployment demonstrate its feasibility and early usability, suggesting potential for wider adoption in environments where knowledge sharing and reuse are critical but challenging under existing document-based frameworks.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many information systems are built around documents: self-contained units optimised for print production and linear reading. While effective for large-scale dissemination, the document-centric organisation constrains how knowledge can be structured, updated, shared, and reused. Formal approaches address some of these limitations but struggle to achieve widespread contribution and adoption due to their prioritisation of formal structure over other system properties such as human usability and scope. AI systems are reshaping document production, but without providing a unified portable alternative to traditional documents for humans' expression and exchange of knowledge. This paper presents MMM, a data model for knowledge documentation that emerged from the practical needs of interdisciplinary collaborative research, and positioned here within a comparative analysis of the design space of information systems. MMM combines a small set of normative constraints with the expressive freedom of free-text labels. It is designed for interoperability across disciplines, applications and deployments without requiring semantic convergence. A reference implementation and pilot deployment data demonstrate implementability and early usability.

items.title: Researchers propose a constrained, verifiable agent framework using typed JSON configurations for reliable open-web data collection, validated on 138 tasks with low execution time and reusable execution paths [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Making Failure Safe: A Constrained, Verifiable Agent Framework for Open-Web Data Collection
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a constrained, verifiable agent framework to improve the reliability of web data collection by large language models (LLMs). Instead of generating free-form code, the framework uses typed JSON configurations based on a six-type collector taxonomy, combined with template constraints, static execution, and rule-based quality checks. This approach addresses common issues like dependency errors and schema mismatches in web scraping.

The framework was tested on 138 tasks, demonstrating that stable data collection requires detailed constraints beyond initial descriptions. On 80 independently verified tasks, it achieved zero execution-stage LLM token usage and the lowest average execution time, offering a reusable and deterministic process suited for repeated scheduled data collection. These results suggest the framework provides a low-cost, verifiable solution for reliable open-web data gathering.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs and agents can generate web scrapers from natural-language requirements, but direct generation remains unreliable because of dependency errors, broken selectors, schema mismatches, and heterogeneous page structures. We propose a constrained, verifiable agent framework that shifts LLM output from free-form code to typed JSON collector configurations, combining a six-type collector taxonomy, template and utility-function constraints, static Airflow DAG execution, rule-based quality checking, and structured feedback correction. Experiments on 138 tasks show that the taxonomy supports description-based requirement typing, while confirming that stable instantiation requires completing source, field, and execution constraints beyond the initial description. On 80 independently source-verified tasks, the framework runs with zero execution-stage LLM tokens and the lowest average wall-clock time, trading moderate one-shot quality for a reusable, deterministic, and verifiable execution path suited to repeated scheduled collection. These results position the framework as a reusable, low-cost, and verifiable execution path for repeated open-web data collection.

items.title: Researchers develop conflict-free solution-space path-planning algorithm for en-route air traffic control with interpretable displays and efficient conflict detection, tested on Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Solution space path planning for supporting en-route air traffic control
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a conflict-free path-planning algorithm designed to support en-route air traffic control by aligning with air traffic controllers' operational needs. The algorithm emphasizes interpretability and flexibility through solution-space displays, allowing controllers to see all feasible safe actions and adapt to changing optimization goals. It integrates three intent-based conflict detection methods—distance-based, time-interval-based, and zone-based—within a computationally efficient framework to identify safe paths.

Two variants of the solution space path planning algorithm, based on vertex and edge search nodes, were evaluated for speed and solution quality. Testing on scenarios from the Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre's Delta sector showed that the vertex-based variant combined with zone-based conflict detection performed best, computing conflict-free paths in an average of 3.69 milliseconds using a 5 nautical mile grid. This approach aims to enhance decision support for tactical air traffic controllers by providing interpretable, efficient, and practical routing solutions.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As technology advances, many path-planning algorithms have been proposed for Air Traffic Management, yet their operational adoption in tactical control remains limited, revealing a misalignment between algorithmic design priorities and air traffic controllers' needs. This underscores the need for decision-support solutions that are inherently interpretable, computationally efficient, and explicitly designed for human use. Focusing on this design challenge, this study develops a conflict-free path-planning algorithm for en-route Air Traffic Control (ATC) designed to be compatible with two guiding considerations: (1) the interpretability and flexibility offered by solution-space displays, which motivate constructing an algorithm that exposes all feasible safe actions and accommodates shifting optimization goals; and (2) the decision logic controllers naturally apply when enforcing operational constraints, such as separation standards, maneuverability limits, waypoint minimization, and routing practicality. Centered on these principles, the algorithm integrates three intent-based conflict detection methods -- distance-based, time-interval-based, and zone-based -- within a solution-space framework to identify conflict-free paths in computationally efficient ways. Additionally, vertex-based and edge-based search nodes are proposed for solution space path planning (SSPP), resulting in two variants -- SSPPV and SSPPE, respectively, which are evaluated in terms of computational speed and solution quality. Empirical results show that SSPPV paired with zone-based conflict detection achieves the best performance, computing paths in 3.69 ms on average in operational-relevant scenarios based on the Delta sector of the Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre (MUAC) using a 5 nmi grid.

items.title: Researchers introduce RareDxR1, a large language model for autonomous rare disease diagnosis from unstructured clinical notes, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy without human annotation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: RareDxR1: Autonomous Medical Reasoning for Rare Disease Diagnosis Beyond Human Annotation
items.summary:
Researchers have developed RareDxR1, a large language model designed to autonomously diagnose rare diseases directly from unstructured clinical notes. This model addresses limitations of previous AI methods by internalizing fragmented rare disease knowledge and employing a novel training framework that combines knowledge internalization with autonomous evolutionary learning, eliminating the need for structured phenotypes or human annotation. RareDxR1 also introduces Reflection-Enhanced Reasoning Sampling to mimic expert diagnostic reasoning and uses a dual-level curriculum reinforcement learning approach to improve diagnostic accuracy.

Experimental results show that RareDxR1 achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, representing a significant advancement in open-domain rare disease diagnosis. The researchers plan to make their code and dataset publicly available, potentially facilitating further research and development in this critical area of medical AI.

items.originalSummary: arXiv:2607.00147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rare disease differential diagnosis is a critical yet arduous clinical task, requiring physicians to identify precise phenotypes from complex, unstructured patient symptoms and execute intricate reasoning within a vast search space. However, existing AI approaches typically rely on pipeline-based phenotype extraction or retrieval-augmented generation, which suffer from critical information loss due to predefined ontologies, retrieval bottlenecks, and a lack of diagnostic logic. To address these challenges, we introduce RareDxR1, an end-to-end reasoning-centric large language model designed for open-domain rare disease diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes. We design a progressive end-to-end training framework by synergizing knowledge internalization with autonomous evolutionary learning, thereby bypassing reliance on structured phenotypes and closed-set decision-making. To overcome the limitations of RAG and phenotype restriction, we enabled the deep internalization of fragmented rare-disease knowledge directly into the model's parameters. items.title: Researchers introduce a contextual-bandit oversight game modeling two-sided informational asymmetry between human supervisors and AI agents, analyzing oversight gaps and dynamic resolution mechanisms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: A Contextual-Bandit Oversight Game with Two-Sided Informational Asymmetry
items.summary:
Researchers have developed a contextual-bandit oversight game to model the two-sided informational asymmetry between human supervisors and AI agents. In this framework, humans privately know their reward functions while AI agents have private knowledge about the quality of their proposed actions, reflecting real-world scenarios where AI assesses situations beyond human direct observation. The study builds on Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning and the Oversight Game, introducing a play/ask/trust/oversee interface that allows precise one-shot characterizations of oversight dynamics without the complexity of full state transitions.

The analysis identifies a gap between an optimal team strategy and a myopic human oversight rule, revealing a zone where AI knows an action is harmful and shutdown would be beneficial, yet the human supervisor, relying on prior beliefs, opts not to intervene. This oversight gap arises from non-credible communication between AI and humans. The researchers also explore how this gap can diminish over repeated interactions through passive learning and active signaling, despite a delay in oversight responses, offering insights into improving human-AI collaboration and safety in autonomous systems.
